title: Prefill Sieve and Kernel Orchestration: admission jitter-damping & micro-reservoir tail smoothing
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: We observe occasional p99 spikes during mixed small/long request workloads caused by suboptimal admission of short-prefill requests and kernel mismatch at decode time. Existing admission heuristics either over-serialize (increasing median latency) or aggressively coalesce (increasing p99).

Proposal: Implement a two-part system: (1) a lightweight prefill sieve (prefill classifier + short-window jitter-damping) that tags incoming requests for opportunistic coalescing without blocking short-latency traffic, and (2) a kernel orchestration layer that consumes sieve hints (attention-sparsity fingerprints + prefix-length histogram) to pick the most appropriate kernel variant and decode scheduling strategy at admission time. Combine this with a micro-reservoir tail-smoothing mechanism: when the system detects tail pressure, reserve small token-slots for low-latency-prefill flows and opportunistically spill excess into larger batch kernels.

Why unique: This approach separates admission intent (sieve) from execution placement (kernel orchestration), enabling non-blocking short-paths and smarter kernel choices that exploit attention sparsity and prefix homogeneity. Goal: reduce p99 on mixed workloads by ~20-30% while keeping median change <5% and unit cost delta <2%.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for 512-token mixed workload decreases by >=20% in staging compared to baseline run-2026-02-01
median latency change <= +5% for stable traffic profiles
throughput (tokens/sec) maintained within -3% of baseline under sustained load
no regression in model output quality on eval prompt set (production-evals v2) beyond existing variance thresholds
feature gated with rollout flag and automated rollback on error budget breach
end-to-end tests for admission paths and kernel selection added to CI with deterministic mocks
tasks: Design: define sieve signal shape, jitter-damping window, and micro-reservoir sizing (Asha + Diego)
Instrumentation: add sieve telemetry (per-flow tags, coalesce decisions, wait times) and kernel-choice tracing (PR #) (Infra)
Implementation: prefill sieve service (inference-proxy hook) + admission API (Diego)
Implementation: kernel orchestration module that consumes sieve hints and selects kernel variant (Nina)
Micro-reservoir: implement slot reservation and spill policy in admission orchestrator (Diego)
E2E: create staging scenarios (short/long mixed traffic) and baseline runs for comparison (SRE)
Performance: run A/B canary in runtime-1.21 with 10% traffic, monitor p50/p95/p99, cost per token (Perf team)
QA: add synthetic determinism tests and fuzz admission edge cases (QA)
Docs: write design doc + rollout steps in Confluence; annotate console dashboards with new metrics (Docs)
Feature flagging: gate behind experiment flag and include automatic circuit-breaker on SLO breach
updates: 2026-02-12 - Ticket created. Baseline traces attached from incident on 2026-01-28 showing 3 sustained p99 spikes during mixed traffic run.
2026-02-18 - Design review: decided on 8ms jitter-damping window for short-prefill candidates; team preferred soft-reservation (micro-reservoir) vs hard priority to avoid starvation.
2026-02-25 - Kernel vendor review: patched kernel selector API to accept attention-sparsity fingerprints (Nina). Changed fingerprint size to 64-bit hash to reduce RPC size.
2026-03-02 - Prototype: prefill sieve implemented as lightweight hook in inference-proxy; initial micro-reservoir reserve == 6 token-slots per GPU pool. Running local perf harness.
2026-03-05 - Found an edge case where extremely bursty tiny-requests cause reservoir thrash. Added backoff multiplier and per-customer cap to reservoir allocation.
2026-03-08 - Canary plan drafted: 10% traffic runtime-1.21 region us-west-2 for 48h. Success criteria: no SLO error budget burn and p99 improvement >=20%.

2026-03-10 - Pre-canary smoke: unit + CI integration tests passing. Dependency block: kernel-variant mem-stability fix (ENG-801333) needs to ship to enable full canary; mitigated by fallback to baseline kernel for flagged customers.
comments: Diego Rivera (2026-02-20): We should be careful about how sieve tags propagate to multi-tenant pools. Suggest tenant-aware cap to avoid cross-tenant noise.
Nina Patel (2026-02-25): Kernel selector accepts sparsity fingerprint but we need per-kernel warm counts to avoid cold-start kernel penalties. I'll add warm-count heuristics.
SRE on call (2026-03-05): Observed reservoir thrash in stress sim; recommend adding both soft and hard caps to reservoir allocation and a decay window of 30s.
PM feedback (Ravi Kumar, 2026-03-06): Ensure feature flag includes an 'aggressive_coalesce' knob for experiments; product wants ability to toggle cost-vs-latency tradeoffs.
Design review note (2026-03-09): Consider exposing a console heatmap for sieve decisions to help debug customer reports.
